Out of the 4 internal configurations this case is designed for, this one is the most ambitious. It fits a 240mm AIO cooler, full-size GPU, SFX PSU, ITX motherboard, and 2 hard drives all in about 10L of space.

To make sure the cooling is acceptable with all these components crammed into this tiny amount of space, I have conducted a thorough temperature test with this configuration (details here). Compared to an optimal, open-cooling configuration, the !nverse case performed only 8 deg worse for an overclocked i5 (4.4GHz) and 5 deg worse for the R9 390. These are differences in max temperatures while running Prime95 and Unigine Valley.

The next prototype will probably be the one that will be sent to reviewers. Crowdfunding should come after that.

That's it for now. As always, if you have any comments or suggestions regarding anything from case design to prototype testing, please do not hesitate to let me know.

Welcome :)

Anarcho-capitalism is a philosophy based on the idea that markets deliver solutions which are at least as good as government intervention in all circumstances, and better in many. As such, in game theory terms, it's a dominant strategy.

Most ancaps also hold an interest in voluntaryism which is the concept that all political associations should be voluntary. So, for example, a government cannot claim dominion over your property without your explicit consent, and you should be free to secede and form your own if at any point you choose to do so. Most people recognise this right in at least some circumstances without realising it, as many modern nations were formed by seceding from another one, but for some reason they tend to fail to apply that principle to their own government.

Here's a pretty good FAQ

  • Would I be happy in it?: That depends what makes you happy, but the chances are you would given that it would be quite easy to work together with like minded groups to build whatever it is you want in life.

  • How would I get to work? Would I work?: The same way you do now, by applying for a job. Your labour is also your property to sell at whatever price you chose. Alternately you could opt to be self employed or live a subsistance lifestyle. The main difference is that all of your earnings would be yours to decide what to do with.

  • t's honestly hard to imagine such a system, or lack thereof, being stable or peaceful: Why would you expect it not to be peaceful? If you consider the main causes for conflict in the world, they mostly come from groups of people trying to seize control of a government, break away from one or states themselves attempting to expand their terretory. If there's no government to seize, and you can secede just by saying so, then there's much less cause for conflict.
